headline: OccupySaaS movement emerges to rebuild proprietary SaaS as open-source alternatives
summary: A new movement, OccupySaaS, aims to create open-source, drop-in compatible alternatives to existing proprietary SaaS platforms, driven by former employees.
details: The 'OccupySaaS' movement has surfaced, advocating for the development of clean-room, open-source, and drop-in compatible alternatives to widely used proprietary Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions.
This initiative is reportedly fueled by a sentiment among laid-off tech workers, who believe that "infrastructure shouldn't charge rent by the head" and that the current SaaS model is unsustainable.
The movement's core message, "They laid us off. We're rebuilding their SaaS," suggests a direct response to recent industry layoffs, transforming grievances into a collaborative development effort.
The goal is to provide viable, community-driven alternatives that can seamlessly replace existing commercial SaaS offerings, reducing reliance on large tech companies and their subscription models.
caption:
Laid-off tech workers are fighting back. They're launching 'OccupySaaS' to rebuild proprietary software as open-source, drop-in compatible alternatives.

The 'OccupySaaS' movement has surfaced, advocating for the development of clean-room, open-source, and drop-in compatible alternatives to widely used proprietary Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions.

This initiative is reportedly fueled by a sentiment among laid-off tech workers, who believe that "infrastructure shouldn't charge rent by the head" and that the current SaaS model is unsustainable.

The movement's core message, "They laid us off. We're rebuilding their SaaS," suggests a direct response to recent industry layoffs, transforming grievances into a collaborative development effort.

The goal is to provide viable, community-driven alternatives that can seamlessly replace existing commercial SaaS offerings, reducing reliance on large tech companies and their subscription models.

headline_marked: [[LG TV Rooting Vulnerability]] Patched, Limiting Customization Options
headline: LG TV Rooting Vulnerability Patched, Limiting Customization Options
summary: LG has closed a critical vulnerability that allowed users to root their TVs, disabling custom app installations and telemetry control.
details: A user on Hacker News shared methods for rooting LG TVs to enhance privacy and functionality, including disabling telemetry and installing custom apps via Glasshouse.
The process involved rooting the TV, installing Glasshouse to manage telemetry, and then installing desired applications. Users could also restore to factory defaults if needed.
However, LG has reportedly closed the specific vulnerability that enabled this rooting process. This means TVs with firmware released after October 10, 2026, are no longer susceptible.
This patch effectively limits users' ability to customize their smart TVs, disable data collection, and install third-party applications beyond what LG officially supports.
While Dev Mode offers some customization, it does not provide the deep control that rooting allowed. The community hopes for a new exploit to regain these capabilities.
